explanation: A 1494 treaty between Spain and Portugal put the eastern bulge of South America on Portugal's side of a line through the Atlantic. Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas.

claims.text: Portuguese is the official and main language of Brazil.
Spanish, Italian and French are not Brazil's main language.
The Treaty of Tordesillas, signed by Spain and Portugal in 1494, drew a line through the Atlantic that placed the eastern part of South America on Portugal's side.
Brazil is the only country in the Americas whose official language is Portuguese.

writerNotes: Spanish is the trap for players who think of South America as Spanish-speaking; most players know Portuguese, so counterintuitive stays false. Self-check (9.3): lint run clean; every claim listed with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where honest; datasets: mledoze-countries cca3=BRA languages {por: Portuguese}; no other country in region Americas lists por, which supports c4; rival test: Spanish is spoken by all Brazil's Spanish-American neighbours, but not as Brazil's main language; volatility evergreen, no time words, nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026; regional: Brazil is known worldwide; style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words; myths: no match in myths.json; mystery and encore checks: not applicable to a practice item; doubts: none

evidence.restatement: Brazil's main language is Portuguese, not Spanish, Italian or French.
The Treaty of Tordesillas of 1494 set a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands. Land east of it, including the eastern part of South America, fell to Portugal.

claimResults.note: High-risk: knowledge only, so it counts only once a confirming check carries dataset or web evidence (§9.9 rule 3). No pinned dataset states it, and this run had no WebSearch: the shared per-turn search budget was exhausted before its first search ran.

evidence.excerpt: Of the 56 entries with "region": "Americas", only one lists Portuguese: BRA languages {"por":"Portuguese"}

claimResults.note: The dataset lists Portuguese as Brazil's only language, matching the official and main language.

evidence.restatement: Spanish, Italian and French are not Brazil's main language.
The Treaty of Tordesillas of 1494 split the Atlantic world between Spain and Portugal along a line that left the eastern bulge of South America to Portugal.
Brazil is the only country in the Americas with Portuguese as its official language.

claimResults.note: A stable 'only' over a fixed small set; I know of no other American state with Portuguese as an official language.

editor.reason: Reinstated under decisions memo section 18; previous cut: Both checks pass, but high-risk c3 (explanation, date) rests on knowledge alone in both checks. Neither checker could search (the batch used 0 of its 26 searches because the shared search budget was exhausted) and no pinned dataset covers it, so §9.9 rule 3 cannot pass. No wording fix adds evidence, and stepping down the precision ladder changes claims (§9.2), so it is cut. Both checkers found the content sound: redraft it under a new id once web evidence can be gathered. It missed by one claim, so the redraft is cheap.
